static_traits.name: Lin Shan
static_traits.social_status: Good social support (has a group of supportive friends, but has not yet discussed fishing-disappointment emotions with them)
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to Reflect on one's own thinking patterns, high cooperation, calm tone, fairly good logic

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to ignore the positive aspects of fishing trips and focus only on what went wrong, leading to disappointment and frustration.
basic_info.core_demands: Because the disappointment while fishing has affected my overall enjoyment of this hobby and my mood beyond the outings, I have come to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / I am a failure
Only achieving specific goals counts as success, otherwise utterly worthless

special_situations.event: Not catching the desired fish (such as salmon) on a fishing trip, not matching the preset goal
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the specified fish species was not caught, this trip equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Puts all attention and time into achieving a single goal, ignoring positive experiences in the process

special_situations.event: Once spent a whole day trying to catch a big bass, in the end only caught a few small fish
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the catch is not big enough or does not match the plan, it shows my ability is very poor
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Through self-criticism and deprecation, forces themselves to work harder next time, or doubles and sets higher expectations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I wasted time; I am a terrible fisherman.

special_situations.event: Before each trip, sets high expectations for oneself of having to catch specific fish species
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should/must achieve the set goal, otherwise I am not worthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on achieving a specific result, ignoring the environment, experience and other positive outcomes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why bother, better not to go.

special_situations.event: When other activities do not go as planned
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If things have not gone as planned, it shows everything is messed up
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reinforcing self-Demands with negative self-talk, reducing attention to positive aspects
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Failed again, I cannot do anything.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to confirm self-worth and gain a sense of achievement by reaching clear outcomes
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure being seen as incapability, thereby making the whole experience lose meaning and triggering Self-denial
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control by holding high standards, focusing on results and criticizing oneself, avoiding facing the Anxiety brought by failure

object_relations.self_representation: A person who has failed and needs to prove his own worth through grades
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges/internalized external standards (negating me if standards are not met)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking in counseling about an experience of not achieving a fishing goal, or being invited to look back at positive aspects
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating not achieving with being negated, worrying that relaxing standards means losing value (transference: Projecting inner harsh standards onto the counseling situation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, Empathic tone, first validate their disappointment and stress, then invite them to observe evidence, distinguish results from worth, avoid direct refutation or judgment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests lowering goal pressure and focusing on process experience
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing that not holding high standards will make oneself unimportant or looked down on (transference: Introjecting external Demands as absolute rules)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Acknowledges the importance of their standards, while exploring the sources of these standards and the situations where they apply, encouraging them to flexibly adjust rules based on their own experience.

manifestations: Viewing a fishing trip that did not achieve its goal as 'ruined', believing it has no meaning
When results do not match Anticipation, the nature and tranquility in the experience are ignored
outcomes: Low mood, enhanced Sense of frustration
Has a negative impact on mood and motivation for other activities

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Setting fishing goals in a 'must/should' manner (must catch a specific species of fish)
Equating unachieved results with failure, holding rigid standards

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on.
manifestations: Strong Self-deprecation when goals are not achieved (such as 'I am a terrible angler')
Overly sensitive to outcomes, ignoring present experience and positive aspects

exception_events.target_problem: When not catching the desired fish on fishing trips, the client typically focuses only on the negative and develops disappointment and Depression, making it hard to enjoy the process and other positive experiences of the day.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During a fishing trip last year, she did not put too much pressure on herself, enjoyed the process naturally, and felt proud and satisfied after catching a big trout, in a Good mood all day.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different approach and mindset — did not set rigid goals at the time, focusing attention on present experience and enjoyment, hence lower pressure and more salient positive experiences.

positive_force: Having a supportive friend group (although not yet discussed this issue)
Able to be aware of and describe negative automatic thoughts and cognitive patterns
Has had successful fishing experiences and can recall positive feelings
Willing to try using an 'alternative perspective' to restructure thinking and practice gratitude
negative_force: Black-and-white/all-or-nothing thinking leading to equating unachieved goals with failure
Mental filtering and negating the positive causing positive experiences to be ignored
Sets rigid 'should' goals for oneself; the pressure is excessive
Self-deprecation tied to external outcomes binds self-worth, affecting mood and motivation

target_behavior.behavior: Strong disappointment and Self-deprecation (negative self-talk) when fishing does not achieve preset goals
antecedent: Before trips, sets high expectations of catching a specific fish species
Not catching the target fish that day or only catching smaller fish
Long attempts at a specific goal without results
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive distortions (black-and-white thinking, mental filtering, negating the positive) making 'not achieved' seen as 'complete failure', and binding self-worth to results
target_behavior.function: Maintaining high standards and a sense of control through self-criticism, while avoiding facing uncertainty and frustration
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased enjoyment of fishing, Low mood persisting into daily life, affecting enjoyment of and mood toward other activities
